transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having these eating episodes, and afterward I just feel really awful about myself. Like, gross and disappointed, like I should be able to control it better. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s been bothering me enough that I end up writing really harsh things about myself in my journal afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit or do anything else to try to compensate for what you’ve eaten?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that. I mostly just feel bad afterward. I’m not sure if there’s something else you mean by “compensate,” though.
Do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or engage in excessive exercise after eating to try to control your weight or shape?

No, I don’t use laxatives or water pills or anything like that. And I wouldn’t say I exercise excessively after. I mean, sometimes I think, like, “I should be better tomorrow,” but I don’t really do anything like that to make up for it, if that makes sense.
When you’re having one of these eating episodes, do you feel like you can’t stop eating or control what you’re eating?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally out of control, but once I start, it’s like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. Even while I’m thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” I just… don’t really stop until the food is gone, or I feel too uncomfortable. Does that make sense?
Do you judge yourself harshly based on your body shape or weight, even when other people might not see anything wrong?

I’m… not sure. I mean, I don’t love how I look all the time, but I don’t know if I’d say I judge myself harshly exactly. Maybe I’m kind of critical sometimes, like most people are? I don’t want to overstate it.
Would you say that how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself is strongly influenced by your weight or body shape?

I don’t think it’s, like… strongly, no. I mean, if I’m having a bad day with how I look, it can make me feel kind of gross or embarrassed, but I don’t think my whole self-worth is based on it. At least, I hope not. Is that what you mean?
How often do these eating episodes happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week?

Um… yeah, I think it would be at least once a week. Not every single day or anything, but for the past few months there’s usually been one night a week where after work I buy way more food than I need and then just kind of eat it all in one stretch. I can’t really think of a recent month where it stopped for more than maybe a week or so. Is that… the kind of frequency you mean?
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or other activities?

I mean… I still get to my cleaning shifts, and I don’t usually cancel things like design events or anything. So I don’t want to make it sound like my life is falling apart.

But the next day I can feel really distracted and kind of ashamed. And sometimes I put off sketching because I don’t want to open my journal and see what I wrote afterward. That sounds kind of small, maybe, but it does get in the way a little. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel depressed, guilty, or anxious specifically after these eating episodes, even if you’re not sure why?

Yeah… I think that’s actually the main reason I came in. After it happens, I feel really gross and disappointed in myself, like I should’ve been able to stop or have more control.

I don’t always want to admit how bad it feels, because it sounds kind of dramatic, but I’ll write in my journal afterward and it turns into me saying really awful things about myself. Mostly guilt, I guess, and feeling ashamed. Is that what you mean?
When you're in the middle of one of these eating episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of what or how much you're eating, like it's happening automatically and you can't stop it?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because it sounds like I’m making excuses, but once I start, it’s like I just keep reaching for the next thing without really deciding to.

I’ll even be thinking, like, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” or “you don’t need more,” but I don’t actually stop. Usually it’s not until the food is gone, or I feel too uncomfortable to keep going. Is that what you mean by not in control?
During these episodes, do you ever feel like you're completely unable to stop eating, even if you wanted to, as if the eating takes over completely?

Yeah… I guess I wouldn’t say “completely” every single time, but it does feel like it kind of takes over.

Once I start, I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically, even when I’m thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” or I know I should stop. I just… don’t, usually not until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable. Does that make sense?
Do you feel significant distress about your body shape or weight, even if others might not see a problem with it?

Um… I don’t know if I’d call it significant, exactly. I mean, I don’t love how I look all the time, but I kind of thought that was normal?

I guess I haven’t really noticed it being the main thing, like my weight or shape specifically. It’s more just… I feel bad about myself afterward, if that makes sense. But I’m not sure if that counts as what you’re asking.
